faq.q: Which marina is closer to Marbella's old town?
faq.a: Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Marbella) is a 5-minute walk from the old town's Plaza de los Naranjos. Puerto Banús is about 10 minutes by taxi or 6 km west along the Golden Mile.

faq.q: Can I rent a boat from Marbella Marina directly?
faq.a: Our fleet operates exclusively from Puerto Banús. That said, Marbella Marina has several independent operators if you prefer that departure point. We recommend Puerto Banús for its amenities and direct access to the best cruising grounds.

faq.q: What's the cost difference between the two marinas?
faq.a: There is no significant price difference for the same boat type. Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours from Puerto Banús, including skipper, drinks, and VAT.

Puerto Banús has large underground car parks (€2–3/hour) with 24/7 access. Marbella Marina has limited street parking and a small pay-and-display lot. For a stress-free start, we recommend Puerto Banús.

faq.q: Is Puerto Banús too crowded in summer?
faq.a: Puerto Banús is busy in July and August, but the marina is well-managed. You'll find plenty of bars and restaurants for a pre-charter coffee. Our boats depart from a dedicated dock, so you avoid the main footfall.

faq.q: What are the best destinations from each marina?
faq.a: From Puerto Banús, you can reach Cabopino, Cala del Faro, and Estepona within 30 minutes. From Marbella Marina, the eastern coast toward Cala Cortés is more direct. Both offer stunning views of La Concha mountain.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance for either marina?
faq.a: Yes, especially from June to September. We recommend booking at least 2–3 weeks ahead for weekends. Weekday availability is better. Contact us on WhatsApp for real-time availability.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks on board?
faq.a: Yes, you are welcome to bring your own food. We provide water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava as standard. If you prefer a specific menu, we can arrange catering at an extra cost.

data.body_html:
When planning a Marbella boat rental, one of the first decisions is where to depart from: Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Marbella) or the world-famous Puerto Banús. Both are excellent, but they serve different itineraries and vibes. This guide breaks down the practical differences so you can choose the best starting point for your day on the water.

Location and Access

Marbella Marina sits right in the heart of Marbella, a 5-minute walk from the old town and the Golden Mile. It's central, convenient, and surrounded by tapas bars. Puerto Banús, on the other hand, is 6 km west, nestled between the Sierra Blanca mountains and the Mediterranean. It's the glitzy hub of the Costa del Sol, with designer boutiques and Michelin-starred restaurants. Both are easily reachable by taxi (€10–15 from central Marbella).

Our Fleet and Departure Point

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús. That includes the Astondoa 40 (€749/2h), Azimut 39 (€749/2h), and the larger Mangusta 80 (from €4,719/4h). Why Puerto Banús? It offers direct access to the best cruising grounds: Cabopino, Cala del Faro, and Estepona. Plus, the marina has 24/7 parking, easy boarding, and a lively atmosphere to kick off your trip. If you prefer Marbella Marina, we can recommend independent operators there, but our fleet is Banús-based.

Distance to Popular Destinations

DestinationFrom Puerto BanúsFrom Marbella Marina
Cabopino15 min30 min
Cala del Faro20 min40 min
Estepona30 min50 min
Cala Cortés45 min25 min
Marbella coastline10 min5 min

The table shows the trade-off: Puerto Banús is better for western destinations; Marbella Marina for eastern ones. Your choice depends on whether you want to explore the Cabopino–Estepona strip or head east toward Cala Cortés and beyond.

Cost and Practicalities

Boat rental prices are similar from both marinas for comparable boats. Our Tier A boats start at €749 for 2 hours (skipper, drinks, VAT included). Parking at Puerto Banús costs €2–3/hour; Marbella Marina has limited free parking but fills up fast. Both marinas have showers, toilets, and fuel stations. For a stress-free start, Puerto Banús offers more space and dedicated charter docks.

Which Marina Suits Your Group?

  • Puerto Banús: Ideal for groups wanting a glamorous start, easy parking, and quick access to the western coast. Perfect for sunset cruises toward Estepona.
  • Marbella Marina: Better if you're staying in central Marbella and want a short walk to the boat. Great for a short 2-hour trip along the Marbella coastline.

Either way, the boat experience is the same: a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. The difference is the departure vibe and the first 15 minutes of cruising.

Private vs Shared Charters

All our boats are private charters – you and your group only. No sharing with strangers. This applies regardless of departure point. If you're looking for a shared experience (e.g., a party boat), you'll find those in Puerto Banús, but we don't offer them. Our focus is on quality, private trips for families, couples, and small groups.

Weather and Best Time to Go

The Costa del Sol enjoys 320 sunny days a year. Sea temperatures range from 18°C in May to 26°C in August. Both marinas are sheltered, but Puerto Banús can get choppy in easterly winds (Levante). Marbella Marina is slightly more protected. Check the forecast before booking – we can advise on WhatsApp.

Frequently asked questions

Which marina is closer to Marbella's old town?

Marbella Marina (Puerto Deportivo de Marbella) is a 5-minute walk from the old town's Plaza de los Naranjos. Puerto Banús is about 10 minutes by taxi or 6 km west along the Golden Mile.

Can I rent a boat from Marbella Marina directly?

Our fleet operates exclusively from Puerto Banús. That said, Marbella Marina has several independent operators if you prefer that departure point. We recommend Puerto Banús for its amenities and direct access to the best cruising grounds.

What's the cost difference between the two marinas?

There is no significant price difference for the same boat type. Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours from Puerto Banús, including skipper, drinks, and VAT.

Which marina has better parking?

Puerto Banús has large underground car parks (€2–3/hour) with 24/7 access. Marbella Marina has limited street parking and a small pay-and-display lot. For a stress-free start, we recommend Puerto Banús.

Is Puerto Banús too crowded in summer?

Puerto Banús is busy in July and August, but the marina is well-managed. You'll find plenty of bars and restaurants for a pre-charter coffee. Our boats depart from a dedicated dock, so you avoid the main footfall.

What are the best destinations from each marina?

From Puerto Banús, you can reach Cabopino, Cala del Faro, and Estepona within 30 minutes. From Marbella Marina, the eastern coast toward Cala Cortés is more direct. Both offer stunning views of La Concha mountain.

Do I need to book in advance for either marina?

Yes, especially from June to September. We recommend booking at least 2–3 weeks ahead for weekends. Weekday availability is better. Contact us on WhatsApp for real-time availability.

Can I bring my own food and drinks on board?

Yes, you are welcome to bring your own food. We provide water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava as standard. If you prefer a specific menu, we can arrange catering at an extra cost.
